newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent pressured lower ahead of May expiry.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent pressured lower ahead of May expiry.

text.p: IPE Brent traded lower on Tuesday as a handful of players sought to pressure the market lower ahead of the May contract's expiry, traders said.
May traded 28 cents off at $17.91 a barrel, while June was 13 cents off at $18.21 at 1215 GMT. Traders said one player appeared to have sold some 2,500 lots of the June contract.
"I don't know what they're up to -- I can only presume something's going on in the cash market," another trader said.
Traders noted that despite the downward pressure the market was holding out pretty well, with June finding support in the $18.20-23 region.
"We're seeing a little bit of manipulation," said another trader. "But there are also some positive signs."
He noted that a few medium-term funds were coming back into the market, although longer-term ones were still steering clear.
On the whole, players saw June staying in the $18-$18.50 range throughout the session. A clear break of $18.50 and a closure of the $18.62-$18.77 gap were seen as its chief hurdles.
Traders said the market was keenly awaiting the latest American Petroleum Institute (API) data.
Last week's report showed that in the week ended April 4 U.S. crude oil stocks rose to 309.95 million barrels.
Distillate stock fell 1.04 million barrels to 98.39 million barrels and gasoline stocks 1.22 million barrels to 195.99 million.
Most attention would be on gasoline for signs the driving season was shifting into top gear but distillate figures would also draw attention, traders said.

"Both gasoline and distillate inventories may draw by 1-2 million barrels. Increasing mogas demand ahead of the peak driving season is expected, while the recent cold weather in the U.S. will have postively influenced distillate demand," said GNI's Leslie Nicholas in his daily energy report.
Gas oil was also lower with the May contract 25 cents off at $164.75 a tonne, as it settled back within the parametres of a three month down trend channel.
"It just doesn't seem very comfortable above that $165 level," said one trader.
